\par\vspace{0.25em}\fontsize{8}{8.8}\selectfont\noindent Notes: Products and instruments are grouped for readability; the underlying workbook retains the measure-level descriptions, dates, COICOP codes, and the measure-specific evidence basis. Policy count reports executed country-product entries and distinct policy devices. The distinct count consolidates successive phases or extensions and a single legal measure represented by several product trajectories; for example, Luxembourg's product-specific VAT trajectories count as one policy. Evidence status concerns the information used to quantify the simulated price effect, not the fiscal-cost estimate. Official/administrative denotes a trajectory determined directly from statutory tax rates, regulated tariffs, or official administrative price or bill series. Estimated denotes a trajectory whose magnitude requires an aggregate-equivalent wedge, representative bill, calibrated pass-through, or model-based proxy. An official policy announcement alone is not sufficient for official/administrative status when its price effect must be estimated. Sources: Bruegel Dataset (2021), `National policies to shield consumers from rising energy prices,' version of 26 June 2023; authors' calculations.
